newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta gas reserve additions well below output.
newsitem.headline: Alberta gas reserve additions well below output.

text.p: Alberta's Energy and Utilities Board said on Monday that new natural gas reserves in the western Canadian province were being added at a rate well below production.

The EUB said in its annual reserves report that additions to gas reserves in the province -- Canada's largest for oil and gas production -- replaced only nine percent of the year's production in 1996.
The board's estimates placed Alberta's remaining gas reserves at the end of last year at 48.9 tillion cubic feet, down 3.9 TCF from 1995. Alberta gas production in 1996 was estimated at 4.3 TCF.
Reserve additions in the EUB's report were calculated by adding new gas discoveries, development of existing pools and reassessment of known pools.

It said gas development drilling was down slightly from 1995 and 33 percent from the record level set in 1994. For the third year in a row, gas development drilling surpassed 2,000 wells, said the EUB, Alberta's main energy regulator.
Exploratory gas drilling, meanwhile, was 14 percent lower than in 1995, but still 25 percent higher than the average over the past 10 years.
Exploratory drilling resulted in only a modest addition of 600 million cubic feet of reserves in 1996, the EUB said.
In crude oil, reserve additions replaced 41 percent of Alberta's established conventional reserves, which stood at 2.15 billion barrels at the end of 1996, the board said.
That was a decrease of 8.6 percent or 203 million barrels from 1995.
Oil development drilling hit an all-time record in 1996, exceeding the old record set in 1993 by 20 percent and rising above the 3,000-well level for the first time, the EUB said.
Exploratory drilling for oil was 16 percent higher than in 1995, but 12 percent below the record set in 1994.
The board said new pool discoveries and development of existing pools added 164 million barrels of reserves, while new and expanded enhanced recovery schemes added 38 million barrels.
At the end of 1996, remaining reserves of crude bitumen from mineable developments were 2.27 billion barrels, down 119 million from 1995, the EUB said.
It said the decrease was equal to the annual production of the Syncrude Canada Ltd and Suncor Energy Inc oil sands project combined. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
